definition: A prolonged expression of grief or sorrow.
author: Charles Dickens
quote: Pocket in their play, they always tripped themselves up and tumbled over her,—always very much to her momentary astonishment, and their own more enduring lamentation.
example_sentence: The final whistle was met with loud lamentation from the home fans.
